methodology.tool: .tmp-ux5/tables-hitch.mjs (Playwright + CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate; per-transition frame deltas via requestAnimationFrame, long tasks via PerformanceObserver({entryTypes:['longtask']})); not in the repository, same convention as §19.1/19.7's tabs-jank.mjs
methodology.dist: composeWebCompatibility (wasm branch; the same static bundle also serves the js branch — unaffected by this change, not separately measured)

scenarios.first: fresh page load, click 'Таблицы и схема' immediately (before the 1500ms idle prewarm has had a chance to fire) — the worst case, and the only one 'before' ever has
scenarios.repeat: click into Matrix once, leave to 'Карточки', wait 600ms, then click into Matrix again
scenarios.firstAfterPrewarm: fresh page load, wait 1800ms (past the 1500ms idle prewarm), THEN click 'Таблицы и схема' for the first time — the idle-prewarm's target case; 'before' has no prewarm mechanism, so this scenario there is just 'first' with an extra idle wait, included to show that waiting alone does not help without it

methodology.correctionNote: A prior version of this file's 'before' baseline was NOT actually built from HEAD fb4cdcd — it was re-measured for this correction round by `git stash`-ing the fix's two source files back to HEAD's committed content, rebuilding the distribution from that, measuring, then restoring the fix and rebuilding again for 'after'. The re-measurement reproduces the exact same shape the earlier numbers already showed for 'repeat' (0 long tasks even pre-fix), which is genuine, not a measurement error: switching to Matrix a SECOND time was already cheap even with zero caching and a brand-new DOM subtree every time, because the ~60ms cost is the browser's own one-time layout/style pass over this page's heaviest subtree, paid once per PAGE LIFETIME (font shaping / style-sharing caches internal to the engine), not per DOM node. That finding is exactly why the persistent, deps-keyed keep-alive cache (matrixCache/matrixCacheDeps) this file originally justified was dropped after this round's review — see FlipCardRivePlan.md §19.11: it carried a real correctness bug (a same-route update mid-slide could desync the cache's recorded deps from the live node's actual content — fixed once, then the whole cache was removed instead of re-litigated) for zero measured benefit over a plain 'build once at idle, then always rebuild fresh' design, which is what TrainingWebApp.kt now does.

after_final.label: after-final
after_final.note: Idle prewarm only (build the heavy subtree once at idle, force layout, discard it) — no persistent keep-alive cache. Matrix rebuilds fresh on every single visit, exactly like every other route.

summary.note: Honest re-measurement (correction round): 'first' and 'repeat' are IDENTICAL before/after, by design — 'first' is the one cost nothing can prevent (something must lay the subtree out once), and 'repeat' was never actually a problem, with or without a fix (see methodology.correctionNote) — the persistent cache this file previously used to justify was measuring/patching a hitch that didn't exist there. Only 'firstAfterPrewarm' genuinely improves: 1 long task/~76-100ms max frame before, 0 long tasks/~33-50ms max frame after, entirely from the idle prewarm forcing the browser's one-time layout/style pass early — no DOM caching needed for that improvement either.
